summary: Russian forces reported destroying 123 UAVs daily while Ukrainian attacks targeted infrastructure across southern and northern regions. Ukrainian Armed Forces advanced in Kharkiv, capturing Bely Kolodez and threatening logistics hubs. Zelensky faced domestic political challenges as Fedorov declined a government post amid embezzlement allegations.
key_points: Russian air defenses destroyed 123 UAVs between 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM on July 22, 2026, with additional shootdowns in Leningrad, Voronezh, and Crimea regions. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31824)

Ukrainian forces captured the settlement of Bely Kolodez in Kharkiv region after driving out the 113th Territorial Defense Battalion, enabling potential encirclement of Ukrainian logistics centers. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31824)
Drone attacks on Ukrainian ports Odessa, Chornomorsk, and Nikolaev continued overnight, with strikes on facilities and vessels reported. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31824)
Zelensky offered Fedorov the position of deputy prime minister for technological development, which he declined, instead seeking reinstatement as defense minister. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31846)
Embezzlement of 68 million hryvnias occurred during anti-drone structure construction in the Nikolaev region, involving a 37-year-old company director from Krivoy Rog. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31843)
Maersk ceased operations at Ukrainian ports due to intensified Russian attacks, rerouting vessels to Constanta, Romania. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31837)
FPV drone attacks in Kharkiv damaged a fuel station, injuring five workers at the Немишлянський район заправки. (Source: @UkraineNow/82837)

points: In the Nikolaev region, 68 million hryvnias were embezzled during anti-drone structure construction for an energy facility. Zelensky ranked fourth in Ukrainians' trust ratings according to a Rating Group survey, while former Commander-in-Chief Zaluzhny achieved 70% trust. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31834)
FPV drone attacks on a fuel station in Kharkiv's Немишлянський район destroyed infrastructure and injured five civilian workers. (Source: @UkraineNow/82837)
Maersk announced cessation of operations at Ukrainian ports due to intensified Russian attacks, rerouting vessels to Constanta, Romania. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31837)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces demonstrate sustained offensive capability across multiple fronts, with daily UAV interceptions and coordinated strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Ukrainian advances in Kharkiv threaten key logistics nodes, potentially stretching Russian defensive lines. Domestic Ukrainian political instability under Zelensky may impact military coordination. Russian ballistic weapon threats and targeting of civilian infrastructure indicate escalation risks. Both sides face challenges in maintaining operational momentum amid attrition warfare.
sections.regional_response: European shipping companies like Maersk are adapting operations due to intensified attacks, rerouting vessels to Romanian ports. Ukrainian trust ratings show declining confidence in Zelensky compared to military leadership. Russian media highlights civilian casualties and mobilization numbers to justify operations. International condemnation of attacks on civilian infrastructure continues. Regional governments prepare for increased refugee flows and economic disruption.
sections.intelligence_notes: Ukrainian drone operations show increasing sophistication targeting both military and civilian infrastructure. Russian air defenses effectively counter UAV threats with daily interceptions. Political developments in Kyiv reveal internal governance challenges affecting military leadership. Embezzlement cases indicate potential logistical vulnerabilities in Ukrainian defense projects. Cross-border attacks in Belgorod and Sumy regions suggest coordinated operations testing Russian defensive capabilities.
